text:
maria: Quick heads-up — hit a weird hang in tests when using AsyncClient + our builtin token refresher with anyio(trio) backend. Minimal repro below, can someone confirm?

maria: 
```py
# pytest with anyio backend=trio
from redwood_sdk import AsyncClient

async def test_trio_backend():
    client = AsyncClient(auto_refresh=True)  # default background refresher
    r = await client.get('https://example.com')
    assert r.status_code == 200
```

maria: Behavior: test never finishes — it hangs at the first request. No stack in test output, just silence until pytest kills it.

kevin: Interesting. Does it reproduce with anyio asyncio backend or only trio?

maria: Only when anyio is using trio (pytest -k test --anyio-backend=trio). Asyncio backend works fine.

sam: Any error logs? "Task was destroyed but it is pending"? TLS handshake?

maria: No explicit error. If I enable DEBUG for redwood.sdk.auth I see the refresher task being spawned from import-time loop: "spawned refresher on <loop 0x7f...>" then nothing.

ellie: That sounds like the refresher captured an asyncio loop from import time and later tries to schedule tasks onto it. Trio's anyio backend won't have that loop, so tasks end up stuck. Do we create background tasks with asyncio.get_event_loop() at import?

maria: Yep — code in _token.py does:
```py
# inside TokenRefresher.__init__
self._loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
self._task = self._loop.create_task(self._refresh_loop())
```

sam: Oof. get_event_loop at import/startup is brittle across backends. anyio can swap loop policies and trio doesn't use asyncio loop at all.

kevin: Short workaround: disable background refresher in tests `AsyncClient(auto_refresh=False)` and call explicit await client.refresh_token() where needed.

maria: Workaround works for now, but we should fix in SDK. I can reproduce locally and in CI.

ellie: Proposed fix: create tasks with anyio.create_task_group() or always use asyncio.get_running_loop() from inside an async entrypoint (i.e., defer creating the background task until client.__aenter__ / async init). That avoids capturing wrong loop at import.

sam: Another compatible approach: detect anyio/trio and fall back to scheduling via anyio.from_thread.run or spawn a native task for trio. But that's messy. Deferring startup until __aenter__ is clean.

kevin: +1 on deferring startup. Also add a fast-fail when user tries to use auto_refresh outside an async context (raise helpful error).

maria: I'll open a small PR to move refresher start to AsyncClient.__aenter__ and guard in sync usage. Will include test matrix for anyio backends.

ellie: Thanks — add a changelog note about behavior change and a migration tip (set auto_refresh=False to keep old behavior).

sdk-bot: Created issue #1428: "async refresher: defer task creation to async init to avoid anyio/trio hang". Assigned to maria.

kevin: One more ask — add a tiny repro to our devex samples folder and a mention in the notebook quickstart (common gotcha for Jupyter users using nest_asyncio).

maria: Good call. I'll add sample and a note about notebooks.

sam: Thanks! Saved me several hours of debugging. :relieved:
